items.title: Effect depends on the Editor module, which was removed in Slicer 5

findings.title: Effect depends on the Editor module, which was removed in Slicer 5
findings.explanation: The module registers itself as an Editor extension (`slicer.modules.editorExtensions['CarreraSliceEffect'] = KSliceEffectExtension`, line 1293) and manipulates `slicer.modules.EditorWidget` (line 358) and `EditorLib` (line 3). The Editor module and its editor-extension mechanism were replaced by Segment Editor in Slicer 5, so even after a Python 3 port the effect has no host module and cannot be used.
findings.suggestion: Either target the Segment Editor effect API, or state an explicit Slicer 4.x-only requirement and do not publish for current Slicer.

items.title: No license or copyright terms anywhere in the repository

findings.title: No license or copyright terms anywhere in the repository
findings.explanation: The repository root contains only CMakeLists.txt, README, data/, scripts/ and src/; there is no LICENSE or COPYRIGHT file (confirmed by directory listing and by searching for license/copyright strings). The Slicer-derived headers refer to a COPYRIGHT.txt that is not present, and the README (3 lines) states no terms. Without any license, users and the extension index have no permission to redistribute the extension binaries or source.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (any OSI-approved license compatible with the bundled third-party code) and a COPYRIGHT.txt, and reference it from the README.

items.title: No top-level license for the repository; bundled GPL code and undeclared terms for the extension

findings.title: GPL-3.0 third-party sources bundled without compatible overall terms
findings.evidence:
it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
findings.explanation: `getopt_pp` (duplicated in src/util/getopt/ and src/sfm_local_chanvese/util/getopt/) is GPL-3.0-or-later. It is currently not compiled (neither directory is added by any CMakeLists), but it is distributed in the source tree alongside code with no license at all, which is an inconsistent licensing situation for anyone redistributing the repository.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused GPL sources, or document the mixed licensing explicitly and ensure the extension's own license is GPL-compatible if these files are ever linked.

findings.title: No top-level license for the repository; bundled GPL code and undeclared terms for the extension
findings.evidence:
it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
findings.explanation: The repository has no LICENSE/COPYING file in its listing. It bundles GPLv3 code (getopt_pp in src/util/getopt and src/sfm_local_chanvese/util/getopt), and several Logic sources carry Apache-style headers. Without an explicit license for the extension, the index cannot confirm that distribution to Slicer users is permitted, so the admission requirement for clear distribution permission is not met.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file at the repo root that covers the extension itself, and state how the GPLv3 getopt sources and the Apache-headed sources are licensed in the combined work.

items.title: Scripted module is Python 2 only and cannot be imported in Slicer 5

findings.title: Scripted module is Python 2 only and cannot be imported in Slicer 5
findings.evidence:
if not orient:
        print "Warning, unexpected view orientation!?"
findings.explanation: CarreraSliceEffect.py is the module's only installed script (src/carreraslice_wrap/CMakeLists.txt:12-16) and uses Python 2 print statements throughout (lines 260, 414, 557-558, 726, 800, 809, 836, 840, 1048, 1076, 1102, 1131, 1155) plus `except Exception, e` (line 141) and `xrange` (line 307). Under Slicer 5's Python 3 the file raises SyntaxError at import, so the extension never appears in the Editor and every user who installs it gets a broken module.
findings.suggestion: Port the module to Python 3 (print functions, `except ... as e`, `range`, `slicer.util.arrayFromVolume`) and verify it loads in a current Slicer nightly.

findings.title: Scripted module uses Python 2 syntax and will not load on Python 3 Slicer builds
findings.evidence:
print "Warning, unexpected view orientation!?"
      if event == 'EnterEvent':
findings.explanation: CarreraSliceEffect.py (installed by src/carreraslice_wrap/CMakeLists.txt) uses Python 2 print statements, xrange, has_key, and 'except X, e'. Current Slicer releases run Python 3 only, so the module will fail with SyntaxError when loaded. The target Slicer version is not stated in the entry; the code only works on Slicer 4.x with Python 2.
findings.suggestion: Port the scripted module to Python 3 (print(), range, dict methods, 'except ... as e'), state the supported Slicer versions, and test the module loads in a current Slicer.

items.title: Build uses VTK_USE_FILE, removed in VTK 9 / Slicer 5

findings.title: Build uses VTK_USE_FILE, removed in VTK 9 / Slicer 5
findings.explanation: Slicer 5 ships VTK 9, which no longer defines VTK_USE_FILE; `include(${VTK_USE_FILE})` therefore fails at configure time (empty argument or missing file), so the extension cannot be configured against a current Slicer. The same pattern appears in src/KViewerMain/KSlice_python/CMakeLists.txt:26.
findings.suggestion: Drop the VTK_USE_FILE include and rely on the VTK targets exported by Slicer (`${VTK_LIBRARIES}`), as the rest of the file already does.

items.title: Global compiler flags force-overridden and install prefix pointed at Slicer_DIR

findings.title: Global compiler flags force-overridden and install prefix pointed at Slicer_DIR
findings.explanation: These FORCE-set CMAKE_C_FLAGS/CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS discard the flags Slicer requires (C++ standard, -fPIC on macOS, sanitizer/ABI defines), which can produce binaries that fail to link or load against Slicer's libraries; `LINUX` is not a standard CMake variable so the branch is never taken and the `-Wl,--no-undefined` linker flag is misplaced in compile flags. Line 92 additionally does `set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX ${Slicer_DIR} CACHE PATH ...)`, which can direct extension installs into the Slicer installation tree.
findings.suggestion: Remove the forced flag overrides and the install-prefix override; use `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux"` if platform-specific flags are really needed.

items.title: Logic libraries built without Python wrapping although Python code imports them

findings.title: Logic libraries built without Python wrapping although Python code imports them
findings.explanation: CarreraSliceEffect.py does `import vtkSlicerCarreraSliceModuleLogicPython` (line 485) and `import vtkSlicerFastGrowCutSegmenterModuleLogicPython` (line 444), but neither src/carreraslice_wrap/Logic/CMakeLists.txt nor src/fastGrowCut/Logic/CMakeLists.txt passes WRAP_PYTHON to SlicerMacroBuildModuleLogic. Without wrapping those Python modules are not generated, so the effect fails with ImportError even on a Slicer version where the rest of the code works. I could not read Slicer's macro definition to confirm the default, hence medium confidence.
findings.suggestion: Add WRAP_PYTHON to both SlicerMacroBuildModuleLogic calls (or verify the macro's default in the targeted Slicer version).

items.title: destroy() raises NameError before restoring Editor shortcuts and observers

findings.title: Bare getNode() call in destroy() is not defined in module scope
findings.explanation: `getNode` is a Slicer console convenience, not a name available inside a module file; stopping the bot would raise NameError here and leave the temporary '-UserInput' volume in the scene.
findings.suggestion: Use `slicer.util.getNode(self.uiName)` and check for None before RemoveNode.

findings.title: destroy() raises NameError before restoring Editor shortcuts and observers
findings.explanation: getNode is not imported in CarreraSliceEffect.py (only vtk, qt, ctk, slicer come from __main__). When the KSlice effect is destroyed, the call at line 1224 raises NameError. The code that follows (lines 1227-1233), including the call that reinstalls Editor shortcut keys, never runs, so the Editor's shortcuts stay disabled after the effect is removed and the uiName volume is not removed.
findings.suggestion: Use slicer.util.getNode(self.uiName) (or check for None), and put the shortcut restoration in a try/finally so it runs even if an earlier cleanup step fails.

items.title: force_clean.sh moves the contents of unchecked directories, which can hit root if run without arguments

findings.title: Destructive developer cleanup script committed
findings.explanation: This script moves every file out of two user-supplied directories into /tmp; it is not invoked by the build, but a user running it with the wrong arguments (e.g. a home directory) would lose files. Unquoted `ls` output also breaks on paths with spaces.
findings.suggestion: Remove it from the distributed tree or add argument validation and quoting.

findings.title: force_clean.sh moves the contents of unchecked directories, which can hit root if run without arguments
findings.explanation: The script does not check that $1 and $2 are set. With no arguments, "$1/*" expands to "/*" and the mv moves root-level entries to a temp folder, which can break the system or move user-owned files. Also, the backticked ls output is unquoted, so names with spaces are split.
findings.suggestion: Validate that $1 and $2 are non-empty directories before moving anything, quote the glob expansion, and replace the mv of ls output with a checked loop or rm of build outputs.

items.title: EXTENSION_DEPENDS and build_dependencies do not describe the real build requirements

findings.title: EXTENSION_DEPENDS and build_dependencies do not describe the real build requirements
findings.explanation: The entry lists no build dependencies and src/CMakeLists.txt sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS to "NA", yet the build needs Slicer's CMake macros, VTK, ITK, and the Editor module at runtime (CarreraSliceEffect.py parent.dependencies = ["Editor"]). The index cannot configure the extension from this metadata alone.
findings.suggestion: Set EXTENSION_DEPENDS to the real dependencies (for example Editor/ITK-dependent modules, if any) and list required build dependencies in the catalog entry.

items.title: Editor shortcuts are removed globally when the effect starts and may not be restored

findings.title: Editor shortcuts are removed globally when the effect starts and may not be restored
findings.explanation: KSliceEffectLogic.__init__ calls removeShortcutKeys() on the Editor widget, and only a successful destroy() restores them. Combined with the NameError described above, a user who uses the effect and then closes or reloads the module can be left with Editor shortcuts disabled.
findings.suggestion: Pair the removal with a guaranteed restore in a finally or cleanup path, and document the global side effect.

items.title: Effect monkey-patches Slicer's module namespace and strips global Editor shortcuts

findings.title: Effect monkey-patches Slicer's module namespace and strips global Editor shortcuts
findings.evidence:
if hasattr(slicer.modules, 'editorBot'):
      slicer.modules.editorBot.active = False
      del(slicer.modules.editorBot)
    slicer.modules.editorBot = self
findings.explanation: The bot stores itself on the shared `slicer.modules` object and deletes other extensions' bots (`slicer.modules.FGCEditorBot`, line 157-159), and line 358 removes the Editor's global keyboard shortcuts. These are process-wide side effects that affect other modules while the effect is active; they are scoped to the effect's lifetime but are fragile and can leave Slicer in a modified state if destroy() is not reached.
findings.suggestion: Keep the bot reference on the effect instance and restore shortcuts in a try/finally.

items.title: Hardcoded developer-machine CMake path in the KSlice_python subtree

findings.title: Hardcoded developer-machine CMake path in the KSlice_python subtree
findings.explanation: KSlice_python/CMakeLists.txt adds a path under /home/ikolesov3, which breaks configuration on other machines if the subtree is built. The subtree is not referenced by src/KViewerMain/CMakeLists.txt, so this is probably dead code, but it reveals a personal path and an execute_process echo.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused subtree or replace the hardcoded path with a variable supplied by the user.

items.title: NameError in updateLabelUserInput: ijk/orient/viewName are not in scope

findings.title: NameError in updateLabelUserInput: ijk/orient/viewName are not in scope
findings.explanation: `ijk`, `orient` and `viewName` are locals of testWindowListener (lines 729-731), not of updateLabelUserInput, so this branch raises NameError on the first left click once the KSlice stage is active, aborting the user-input accumulation path.
findings.suggestion: Store the last ijk/orient/viewName on self in testWindowListener and use those here.

items.title: Sample data is fetched from a private host that users cannot reach

findings.title: Sample data is fetched from a private host that users cannot reach
findings.explanation: The only documented data source is an scp command to a university-internal host, and the test DS004 volume is commented out (src/KSegmentor/tests/CMakeLists.txt lines 34-35). A new user cannot reproduce the tests or the demo from the repository alone.
findings.suggestion: Provide a public download URL with checksums (and a license for the data), or ship a small public sample.

items.title: pasteslice uses self.copySliceView before copyslice has set it

findings.title: pasteslice uses self.copySliceView before copyslice has set it
findings.evidence: if self.copySliceView==self.sliceIJKPlane(): #make sure user hasn't move to a different view
findings.explanation: `self.copySliceView` is only assigned in copyslice (line 881); pressing 'V' before 'C' raises AttributeError instead of reporting that nothing has been copied.
findings.suggestion: Initialise self.copySliceView = None in init_kslice and guard the comparison.

items.title: Developer scratch files with personal paths and exec/execfile committed

findings.title: Developer scratch files with personal paths and exec/execfile committed
findings.explanation: sample.slicerrc.py, setUpSlicerDebug.py and setUpSlicerDebugFull.py contain hardcoded personal paths (/Users/pieper/..., /u4/home/ikolesov3/...), `exec`/`execfile` calls and a `slicr_setup` that starts a local server. They are not installed by CMake (only KUtil and CarreraSliceEffect are in MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS), so they do not run for users, but they are shipped in the source tree and could be copied into a user's slicerrc by mistake.
findings.suggestion: Move these to a separate developer/ folder or remove them from the distributed repository.

items.title: Tests reference data files that are not in the repository and are disabled by default

findings.title: Tests reference data files that are not in the repository and are disabled by default
findings.evidence:
set(KSlice_Angry FALSE CACHE BOOL FALSE) #dont want errors if user doesnt have Boost installed
if(KSlice_Angry)
  add_subdirectory(tests)
endif()
findings.explanation: The only C++ tests are behind an off-by-default flag and point at ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../data/DS004.mha, which is not present in the tree (only DS004_Label0.mha is), so there is no automated verification of the segmentation engines.
findings.suggestion: Add a small committed test volume and enable a smoke test in the default build.
